question:
Which of the following rulers mobilise a large standing army in Delhi due to the Mongol invasion, which posed a huge administrative challenge?
I. Alauddin Khalji
II. Muhammad Tughluq
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughluq maintained a large standing army (विशाल स्थायी सेना) in Delhi mainly to defend the Sultanate against repeated Mongol invasions.

• Alauddin Khalji introduced strict market/price control regulations so that he could pay a huge standing army at low salaries.

• Muhammad bin Tughluq too kept a massive army, which put an enormous burden on the treasury and administration.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Alauddin Khalji (1296–1316) belonged to the Khalji dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

• Muhammad bin Tughluq (1325–1351) of the Tughluq dynasty is famous for experiments like the transfer of capital to Daulatabad and token currency.

• Alauddin introduced the practice of branding of horses (dagh) and descriptive roll of soldiers (chehra).

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete — it names only Alauddin Khalji, whereas Muhammad bin Tughluq also kept a large standing army.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete — it names only Muhammad bin Tughluq, ignoring Alauddin Khalji.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both rulers did in fact maintain a large standing army.

question: In which of the following are the songs of Alvar saints compiled?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Divya Prabandham.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The devotional songs of the Alvar saints (Vaishnava devotees of Vishnu) are compiled in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham (दिव्य प्रबंधम्).

• It is a collection of 4,000 Tamil verses composed by the twelve Alvars.

• It was compiled by Nathamuni and is often called the 'Tamil Veda'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Alvars promoted Bhakti towards Lord Vishnu, while the Nayanars were devotees of Lord Shiva.

• The Bhakti movement in South India (6th–9th century CE) was spearheaded by these Alvar and Nayanar saints.

• Famous Alvars include Andal (the only woman Alvar), Nammalvar and Periyalvar.

NOTE

• Ettutogai (Option 2): An anthology of eight collections of classical Tamil Sangam poetry, not Alvar hymns.

• Tipitaka (Option 3): The canonical collection of Buddhist scriptures written in Pali.

• Adi-Purar / Adi Purana (Option 4): A Jain text dealing with the life of the first Tirthankara Rishabhanatha.

question: Which of the following is a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
option_2: To vote in the Lok Sabha election
option_3: To educate child up to 18 years of age
solution_text:
The correct answer is To protect the natural environment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To protect and improve the natural environment (प्राकृतिक पर्यावरण की रक्षा करना) including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(g).

• Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IV-A, Article 51A of the Constitution.

• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Originally 10 Fundamental Duties were added; the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th duty relating to education of children aged 6–14 years.

• Fundamental Duties are borrowed from the Constitution of erstwhile USSR.

• They are non-justiciable, i.e., not enforceable by courts.

NOTE

• To pay taxes on time (Option 1): A civic obligation, but not listed as a Fundamental Duty in Article 51A.

• To vote in the Lok Sabha election (Option 2): A constitutional/political right, not a Fundamental Duty.

• To educate child up to 18 years of age (Option 3): The duty (Art. 51A-k) relates to providing education opportunities to children between 6 and 14 years, not up to 18 years.

question: Which of the following amendment act of the Indian constitution made Sikkim a full-fledged State of the India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 36th Amendment act, 1975.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 36th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975 (36वां संशोधन अधिनियम, 1975) made Sikkim a full-fledged 22nd State of the Indian Union.

• Sikkim was added to the First Schedule and given seats in Parliament through this amendment.

• Earlier, the 35th Amendment Act, 1974 had made Sikkim an 'associate state' of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sikkim's first Chief Minister was Kazi Lhendup Dorji.

• Sikkim shares borders with Nepal, Bhutan and China (Tibet).

• Article 371F contains special provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim.

NOTE

• 38th Amendment Act, 1975 (Option 1): Made the declaration of Emergency by the President immune from judicial review.

• 35th Amendment Act, 1974 (Option 2): Gave Sikkim the status of an associate state, not a full state.

• 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 (Option 3): The 'Mini-Constitution' that added the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble and the Fundamental Duties.

question: As of 31st July 2025, which of the following country is the member of SAARC?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Afghanistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Afghanistan (अफ़ग़ानिस्तान) is one of the eight member countries of the SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation).

• SAARC was established on 8 December 1985 in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

• Afghanistan joined SAARC as its 8th member in 2007.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The eight SAARC members are: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

• The headquarters/Secretariat of SAARC is located in Kathmandu, Nepal.

• Observer states include the USA, China, Japan, EU, Iran, etc.

NOTE

• Iraq (Option 2): A West Asian country and member of the Arab League, not SAARC.

• UAE (Option 3): A Gulf/West Asian nation, member of the GCC, not SAARC.

• Egypt (Option 4): A transcontinental African/Arab country, not a SAARC member.

question: In which sport did Praveen Kumar Sobti won medals at the Asian Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Discus throw.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Praveen Kumar Sobti won Asian Games medals in Discus throw (डिस्कस थ्रो), an athletics field event.

• He won the gold medal in discus throw at the 1966 Bangkok Asian Games and again at the 1970 Bangkok Asian Games.

• He was also a Commonwealth Games medallist in the discus throw.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Praveen Kumar Sobti was also a famous actor, best remembered for playing Bhima in B. R. Chopra's TV serial Mahabharat.

• The discus throw is a track and field throwing event.

• He also represented India in the 1968 and 1972 Olympic Games.

NOTE

• Long jump (Option 1): A horizontal athletics jumping event; not the sport in which Sobti competed.

• Shooting (Option 2): A precision target sport, unrelated to Sobti.

• Wrestling (Option 4): A combat sport; Sobti was a thrower, not a wrestler.

question: Who has been appointed as the Chairperson of Fertilizer Association of India (FAI) in June 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sailesh C. Mehta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sailesh C. Mehta (शैलेश सी. मेहता) was elected/appointed as the Chairman of the Fertiliser Association of India (FAI) in June 2025.

• He is the Managing Director of Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd.

• The FAI (भारतीय उर्वरक संघ) is the apex body of the Indian fertiliser industry.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Fertiliser Association of India (FAI) was established in 1955 and is headquartered in New Delhi.

• FAI works for the development of the fertiliser industry, agriculture and allied sectors.

• It publishes fertiliser statistics and organises the annual FAI Seminar.

NOTE

• T. Rabi Sankar (Option 1): A Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

• S. Mahendra Dev (Option 2): A noted economist, former Director of IGIDR and ex-Chairman of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).

• Prashant Kumar (Option 4): A banker, best known as the MD & CEO who led the restructuring of YES Bank.

question: As of July 2025, who is the Chairperson of the Lok Sabha Estimates Committee?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanjay Jaiswal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sanjay Jaiswal (संजय जायसवाल) was named the Chairperson of the Lok Sabha Estimates Committee (लोकसभा प्रावकलन समिति).

• He is a BJP Member of Parliament from Paschim Champaran (Bihar).

• The Estimates Committee examines the estimates included in the Budget and suggests economies in expenditure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha; no member from the Rajya Sabha.

• It is known as the 'Continuous Economy Committee'.

• The first Estimates Committee (1950) was headed by John Mathai.

NOTE

• Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Option 1): A JD(U) leader (Lalan Singh) serving as a Union Cabinet Minister.

• Nishikant Dubey (Option 3): A BJP MP from Godda (Jharkhand), known for chairing other committees, not the Estimates Committee here.

• Om Birla (Option 4): The Speaker of the Lok Sabha, who nominates committee members but does not chair the Estimates Committee.

question: In December 2024, the Union Health Minister said that the TB incidence rate in India has decline to _____ per 100000 population in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 195.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In December 2024, Union Health Minister J. P. Nadda stated that India's TB incidence rate had declined to 195 per 1,00,000 (195 प्रति एक लाख) population in 2023.

• This marked a reduction of about 17.7% since 2015 (from 237 to 195 per lakh).

• India aims to eliminate TB ahead of the global SDG target of 2030.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The programme for TB elimination is the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP).

• TB is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

• World Tuberculosis Day is observed on 24 March.

NOTE

• 222 (Option 1): An incorrect figure; not the 2023 incidence rate quoted by the minister.

• 312 (Option 3): Does not match the official 2023 TB incidence data.

• 316 (Option 4): An incorrect value that overstates the TB incidence rate.

question: During the Union Budget for 2025-26, it was announced that the government will introduce a Rs _____ crores term loan scheme.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2025-26, the government announced term loans up to Rs 2 crore (2 करोड़ रुपये) for first-time entrepreneurs.

• This new scheme targets 5 lakh women, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe first-time entrepreneurs over the next 5 years.

• The Budget 2025-26 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Budget 2025-26 raised the nil income-tax slab limit to an income of Rs 12 lakh under the new regime.

• A new Income Tax Bill was proposed to simplify direct taxation.

• The scheme incorporates lessons from the Stand-Up India Scheme.

NOTE

• 8 (Option 1): Not the term-loan amount announced in the Budget 2025-26.

• 6 (Option 2): Incorrect; does not match the Budget announcement.

• 5 (Option 4): Refers to the number of lakh beneficiaries, not the loan amount in crores.

question: World Poverty Clock Report is released by which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is World Data Lab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The World Poverty Clock is developed and released by the World Data Lab (वर्ल्ड डेटा लैब).

• It provides real-time poverty estimates across countries and the world.

• The organisation is based in Vienna, Austria.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The World Poverty Clock tracks progress towards the UN Sustainable Development Goal 1 (No Poverty).

• It uses publicly available data on income and consumption.

• It measures those living in extreme poverty (below the international poverty line).

NOTE

• World Bank (Option 2): Releases reports like the World Development Report and Ease of Doing Business (earlier), not the World Poverty Clock.

• UNDP (Option 3): Publishes the Human Development Report and the Multidimensional Poverty Index (with OPHI).

• IMF (Option 4): Releases the World Economic Outlook and Global Financial Stability Report.

question: Who was India's first-ever gold medallist at the Asian Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sachin Nag.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sachin Nag (सचिन नाग) won India's first-ever gold medal at the Asian Games.

• He won the gold in the 100 metres freestyle swimming event at the first Asian Games, held in New Delhi in 1951.

• The 1951 Asian Games were the inaugural edition of the Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The first Asian Games (1951) were held at the National Stadium, New Delhi.

• India finished second in the medal tally at the 1951 Asian Games.

• The Asian Games are organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).

NOTE

• KD Jadhav (Option 1): India's first individual Olympic medallist (bronze in wrestling at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics).

• PT Usha (Option 3): The 'Golden Girl' / 'Payyoli Express' of Indian athletics, a later Asian Games multiple gold medallist, not the first.

• Kanti Shah (Option 4): Not associated with Asian Games athletics (a film director); a distractor option.

question: Surya Namaskar term is related to which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yoga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation) is a term related to Yoga (योग).

• It is a sequence of 12 yogic postures (asanas) performed in a flowing series.

• It is traditionally practised at sunrise, facing the sun.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• International Yoga Day is celebrated on 21 June every year.

• Yoga finds mention in ancient texts, and Patanjali is regarded as the father of yoga for his Yoga Sutras.

• Surya Namaskar improves flexibility, strength and blood circulation.

NOTE

• Cricket (Option 2): A bat-and-ball team sport; unrelated to Surya Namaskar.

• Lawn Tennis (Option 3): A racquet sport, not connected with the term.

• Basketball (Option 4): A court-based team sport; not related to yoga postures.

question:
The Aravalli Green wall Project covers which of the following state?
I. Delhi
II. Bihar
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Aravalli Green Wall Project (अरावली ग्रीन वॉल परियोजना) covers Delhi among the given options, but not Bihar.

• The project aims to create a green buffer/wall along the Aravalli hill range to combat land degradation and desertification.

• It spans four states around the Aravalli range: Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Gujarat.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It was launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

• The initiative is inspired by Africa's Great Green Wall project in the Sahel region.

• It plans a 5 km wide green belt covering the Aravalli landscape.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Wrong, because Bihar is not part of the Aravalli Green Wall Project.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, since Bihar (statement II) is not covered.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as Delhi (statement I) is indeed covered by the project.

question: Which country will host the International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) World Cup in 2027?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India (भारत) will host the ISSF (International Shooting Sport Federation) World Cup in 2027.

• India will also host the ISSF Junior World Championships in 2028.

• This decision was announced by the ISSF, boosting India's status in world shooting.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The ISSF is headquartered in Munich, Germany.

• The National Rifle Association of India (NRAI) is the governing body for the sport in India.

• India also hosted the ISSF Junior World Cup for the first time in 2025.

NOTE

• France (Option 2): Not the announced host of the 2027 ISSF World Cup.

• England (Option 3): Not selected to host the 2027 event.

• Germany (Option 4): Home of the ISSF headquarters, but not the host of the 2027 World Cup.

question: Who is the author of the book 'Development as Freedom'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amartya Sen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The book 'Development as Freedom' was written by the economist Amartya Sen (अमर्त्य सेन).

• The book argues that freedom is both the primary end and the principal means of development.

• It was published in 1999.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Amartya Sen won the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998 for his work on welfare economics.

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

• His other works include 'The Argumentative Indian' and 'Poverty and Famines'.

NOTE

• Durjoy Datta (Option 1): A popular Indian novelist known for romance fiction, not this book.

• Bhisham Sahni (Option 2): A Hindi writer, famous for the novel 'Tamas'.

• Vivek Shanbhag (Option 4): A Kannada writer, known for the novel 'Ghachar Ghochar'.

question: Which of the following festival is NOT celebrated in Rajasthan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karaga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Karaga (करगा) is NOT a festival of Rajasthan; it is a traditional festival of Karnataka.

• Bengaluru Karaga is one of the oldest festivals of Karnataka, dedicated to the goddess Draupadi (Shakti).

• Teej, Gangaur and Makar Sankranti are all celebrated in Rajasthan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Teej and Gangaur are among the most important festivals of Rajasthan celebrating marital bliss and the goddess Parvati/Gauri.

• Rajasthan is also famous for the Pushkar Fair and the Desert Festival of Jaisalmer.

• Karaga is performed by the Thigala community of Karnataka.

NOTE

• Teej (Option 1): A monsoon festival widely and grandly celebrated in Rajasthan.

• Gangaur (Option 2): A major Rajasthani festival honouring Gauri (Parvati).

• Makar Sankranti (Option 4): A harvest/kite festival celebrated across Rajasthan and India.

question: Which Mauryan architectural structure is famous for its beautiful, sculpted gateways?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanchi Stupa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sanchi Stupa (सांची स्तूप) is famous for its beautifully sculpted gateways (toranas).

• The Great Stupa at Sanchi was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.

• It is located in Madhya Pradesh and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The stupa has four ornately carved toranas (gateways) facing the four cardinal directions.

• The carvings depict scenes from the Jataka tales and the life of the Buddha.

• A stupa is a hemispherical Buddhist structure containing relics.

NOTE

• Amaravati Temple/Stupa (Option 2): A Buddhist site in Andhra Pradesh of the Satavahana period, not the Mauryan gateway example asked here.

• Ajanta Caves (Option 3): Rock-cut caves in Maharashtra famous for Buddhist paintings and murals, dating to the Satavahana/Vakataka periods.

• Nalanda University (Option 4): An ancient centre of learning in Bihar, established later during the Gupta period.

question: In April 2025, who developed India's first genome edited rice varieties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ICAR.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research) (आई.सी.ए.आर.) developed India's first genome-edited rice varieties.

• The two varieties are 'DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala)' and 'Pusa DST Rice 1'.

• These were developed using genome-editing (CRISPR-based) technology for higher yield and stress tolerance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• ICAR is headquartered in New Delhi and functions under the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare.

• 'DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala)' was developed by ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad.

• 'Pusa DST Rice 1' was developed by ICAR-IARI, New Delhi.

NOTE

• IARI (Option 1): The Indian Agricultural Research Institute (Pusa Institute) is an institute under ICAR; the achievement is credited to ICAR as the apex body.

• NIPGR (Option 3): The National Institute of Plant Genome Research, a plant genomics research body, but not credited with these rice varieties.

• IRRI (Option 4): The International Rice Research Institute, based in the Philippines, an international body, not the Indian developer.

question: In October 2024, DRDO developed the 'VSHORADS' system. What is it used for?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Short-range air defence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• VSHORADS (Very Short Range Air Defence System) (कम दूरी की वायु रक्षा) is used for short-range air defence.

• It is a man-portable air defence system (MANPADS) designed to neutralise low-altitude aerial threats at short ranges.

• It was developed by the DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• VSHORADS uses a dual-band infrared imaging seeker (IIR) for target tracking.

• It is designed to be light-weight and shoulder-fired, ideal for quick deployment.

• DRDO is headquartered in New Delhi and functions under the Ministry of Defence.

NOTE

• Underwater mining (Option 1): A seabed resource-extraction activity, unrelated to VSHORADS.

• Missile fuel storage (Option 2): Not the function of VSHORADS, which is a launch/defence weapon system.

• Submarine communication (Option 4): Handled by dedicated naval communication systems, not by an air-defence missile.

question: Who among the following established close relations with the French and modernized his army with their help?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tipu Sultan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tipu Sultan (टीपू सुल्तान) established close relations with the French and modernised his army with their help.

• He was the ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore and was known as the 'Tiger of Mysore'.

• He used French support and technology to strengthen his forces against the British.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Tipu Sultan was a pioneer in the use of iron-cased rockets (Mysorean rockets) in warfare.

• He was killed defending Srirangapatna in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799).

• He planted the 'Tree of Liberty' and became a member of the Jacobin Club.

NOTE

• Mahadji Shinde (Option 1): A powerful Maratha chief of Gwalior who modernised his army with the help of Benoit de Boigne, but the classic example asked is Tipu.

• Ali Wardi Khan (Option 2): The Nawab of Bengal (grandfather of Siraj-ud-Daulah), not associated with French-modernised army.

• Shah Alam II (Option 4): A weak Mughal emperor, granted the Diwani of Bengal to the British in 1765.

question: Which of the following article of the Indian constitution states that there shall be a Vice-President of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 63.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 63 (अनुच्छेद 63) of the Indian Constitution states that 'There shall be a Vice-President of India.'

• The Vice-President is the second-highest constitutional office in the country.

• The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (Article 66).

• The Vice-President holds office for a term of 5 years.

• India's first Vice-President was Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.

NOTE

• Article 62 (Option 1): Deals with the time of holding election to fill a vacancy in the office of the President.

• Article 68 (Option 3): Deals with the time of holding election to fill a vacancy in the office of the Vice-President.

• Article 65 (Option 4): Provides that the Vice-President shall act as President during a casual vacancy in the office of the President.

question: Who was Prime Minister of India during Eighth five year plan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is P.V. Narsimha Rao.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• P. V. Narasimha Rao (पी.वी. नरसिम्हा राव) was the Prime Minister of India during the Eighth Five Year Plan (1992–1997).

• The Eighth Plan is associated with the era of economic liberalisation (LPG reforms of 1991).

• Its main focus was on human resource development, employment and growth.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Eighth Five Year Plan was delayed by two years (originally 1990–95) due to political and economic instability.

• Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister during this period who launched the reforms.

• Five Year Plans in India were formulated by the erstwhile Planning Commission.

NOTE

• Morarji Desai (Option 1): India's first non-Congress PM (1977–79); the Fifth Plan period, later followed by a plan holiday.

• Indira Gandhi (Option 2): PM during earlier plans (Fourth, Fifth and Sixth), not the Eighth.

• Chaudhary Charan Singh (Option 3): A short-tenure PM (1979–80), not associated with the Eighth Plan.

question: The biological catalysts which help in the breakdown of food in humans known as _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Enzymes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Enzymes (एंजाइम) are the biological catalysts that help in the breakdown of food during digestion.

• They speed up biochemical reactions without being consumed themselves.

• Digestive enzymes like amylase, pepsin, trypsin and lipase break down carbohydrates, proteins and fats.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Most enzymes are proteins in nature and are highly specific to their substrates.

• Amylase (in saliva) digests starch; pepsin (in the stomach) digests proteins.

• Enzyme action is affected by temperature and pH.

NOTE

• Lymph (Option 1): A colourless fluid that is part of the lymphatic/immune system, not a digestive catalyst.

• Mucus (Option 2): A protective secretion that lubricates and shields the lining of organs, not a catalyst.

• Bile (Option 4): A secretion of the liver that emulsifies fats but is not an enzyme (it contains no digestive enzymes).

question: Which two languages flourished alongside Sanskrit in Vedic ancient India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pali and Prakrit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pali and Prakrit (पाली और प्राकृत) were the two languages that flourished alongside Sanskrit in ancient India.

• Prakrit was the language of the common people, while Sanskrit was the language of scholars and rituals.

• Pali was the language in which the early Buddhist scriptures (Tipitaka) were written.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lord Buddha preached mainly in Pali/Prakrit to reach the common people.

• Lord Mahavira (Jainism) spread his teachings in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit.

• These are all Indo-Aryan languages of ancient India.

NOTE

• Hindi and Urdu (Option 1): Modern Indo-Aryan languages that developed much later, in the medieval/modern period.

• Bengali and Tamil (Option 3): Bengali is a later Indo-Aryan language, and Tamil is a Dravidian language, not part of the Vedic Sanskrit era.

• English and Persian (Option 4): Foreign languages introduced in India during the medieval (Persian) and colonial (English) periods.
